<result>Done. Summary below.

## SQL shape chosen

`commitTargetRef` selection is now a join against a de-duplicated set of qualifying commit sequences, resolved through the target index, replacing the correlated `EXISTS` in the outer `WHERE`:

```sql
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT target_effect.sequence AS sequence
  FROM occasion_effects target_effect
  WHERE target_effect.domain_id COLLATE "C" = $d
    AND target_effect.target_ref COLLATE "C" = $ref
    [AND target_effect.sequence &gt;= $after.sequence::numeric]
    [AND target_effect.sequence &lt;= $before.sequence::numeric]
) commit_target ON commit_target.sequence = e.sequence
```

Why this and not `IN (SELECT …)`: both reach the target index, but `IN` plans as a blocking `HashAggregate` + full `Sort`, so a page still costs the Yi's whole history. The `DISTINCT` subquery plans as a streaming `Unique` over the index's own order, feeding a nested loop and an `Incremental Sort` — the pipeline stops as soon as `LIMIT` is satisfied. `DISTINCT` is required for correctness, not just cost: a commit may legally carry the same target on two effects (`decodeOccasionEffects` allows it when the second `beforeHash` continues the first `afterHash`), and without it every sibling row would be duplicated.

Both cursor bounds are restated inside the lookup. They are implied by the outer bounds, so results are unchanged, but they turn the caller's forward paging from O(history-so-far) per page into O(page).

`observations` and `countObservations` now share one `observationSource(sql, normalized)` builder, so a count can no longer select a different set than the page it counts. Ordering, limit, and all other filters are byte-for-byte the previous fragments.

**Key discovery — the `COLLATE "C"` is load-bearing.** `occasion_effects_target_position_idx` is declared `(domain_id COLLATE "C", target_ref COLLATE "C", …)`. PostgreSQL matches an index only when the comparison's collation OID equals the index's, and a plain `col = $1` carries the *default* collation OID even when the database's default collation is itself `C` (this one is). Without naming the collation, the target index is unreachable — the premise that the old `targetRef` path "was narrow" does not hold.

## Before / after EXPLAIN

40,000 commits / 80,000 effects in one Domain; target on 100 of them; `limit 1000`; PostgreSQL 14.17, default planner settings.

**Before** — 43.1 ms, 3290 buffers, 80,900 rows discarded:
```
Limit -&gt; Sort -&gt; Nested Loop -&gt; Nested Loop
  -&gt; HashAggregate
       -&gt; Seq Scan on occasion_effects commit_target
            Filter: ((domain_id = 'dom_busy') AND (target_ref = 'yi:hot'))
            Rows Removed by Filter: 80900
            Buffers: shared hit=2484
  -&gt; Index Scan using occasion_commits_pkey
  -&gt; Index Scan using occasion_effects_domain_id_sequence_ordinal_key on e
Execution Time: 43.136 ms
```

**After** — 1.0 ms, 805 buffers, nothing discarded:
```
Limit -&gt; Incremental Sort (Presorted Key: e.sequence) -&gt; Nested Loop -&gt; Nested Loop
  -&gt; Unique
       -&gt; Index Only Scan using occasion_effects_target_position_idx on target_effect
            Index Cond: ((domain_id = 'dom_busy') AND (target_ref = 'yi:hot'))
            Buffers: shared hit=5
  -&gt; Index Scan using occasion_commits_pkey
  -&gt; Index Scan using occasion_effects_domain_id_sequence_ordinal_key on e
Execution Time: 1.035 ms
```
Deep-page case (`after` at sequence 20000): index cond becomes `(domain_id, target_ref, sequence &gt;= 20000)`, 35 buffers total — the page costs its own length.

Cost no longer scales with Domain size: the driving scan touched 5 buffers instead of 2484, and grows with the Yi's own history only.

## Gate added

`packages/server/src/pg-storage-hot-path-indexes.integration.test.ts` — `plans commit-target observation reads through the target index`. Defect class: reading one Yi's history scans the whole Domain. Who acts: whoever changes the Occasion observation reader.

It drives the real `createPgOccasionObservationReader` through a `debug`-hooked connection, captures the exact statements it emits for both `observations` and `countObservations`, and `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`s them — so it detects production drift rather than a copy of the query kept in the test. A new `effectLogBounds` helper reports which columns bound each `occasion_effects` scan; the law asserted is `['domain_id, sequence', 'domain_id, target_ref']` — no scan of the effect log may be bounded by `domain_id` alone. Verified it fails against the old query (`['', 'domain_id, sequence']` — an unbounded scan) and passes after. No `check:*` name added, so the budget is untouched.

Also added `paged commit target selection matches the in-memory reader effect for effect` to `occasion-commit-log-pg.integration.test.ts`: commits the same four commits to both the PG store and `createMemoryOccasionAtomicStore`, then pages with `limit: 2` and compares each page deep-equal, plus a `before`-bounded query and the counts. Covers the duplicate-target-in-one-commit case and the pushed-down cursor bounds; verified it goes red when `DISTINCT` is dropped. `preparedCanonicalEffect` now derives `canonicalBeforeState` from `effect.beforeHash` instead of hardcoding `null` (no change for the pre-existing test, whose effects all have a null before-hash).

## Item 4 — `commitTargetRef` validation

No change, and that is the consistent call. `normalizeObservationQuery` validates exactly the unbranded string axes (`eventOwner`, `eventName`, `eventNamePrefix`, the committedAt instants, the caller). It does not validate `domainId` or `targetRef` — those are branded (`DomainId`, `OccasionOpaqueReference`) and carry their contract in the type. `commitTargetRef` is the same brand, so re-validating it would invent a stricter contract than `targetRef` has and than the brand implies. I only exported the `NormalizedObservationQuery` interface so the shared query builder can take it.

## Commands and results

```
pnpm typecheck                                    -&gt; clean
pnpm typecheck:tests                              -&gt; 0 test-inclusive type errors
PG_URL=postgres:///bonfire_plan49_test npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts \
  packages/server/src/occasion-commit-log-pg.integration.test.ts \
  packages/server/src/pg-storage-hot-path-indexes.integration.test.ts
  -&gt; 2 files passed, 35 tests passed (18 + 17)
```
Smoke-tested adjacent PG suites that drive the reader through product paths: `normalized-contexts-pg`, `normalized-occasion-recovery-pg`, `kit-install` — 3 files, 18 tests, all passed. The existing `commit target selection returns every sibling effect from the indexed commit` passes unchanged. Nothing committed; `git status` shows only the four files I own. The scratch schema I used for the EXPLAIN work was dropped.

## Out of scope, flagged

I deliberately left the outer `targetRef`, `eventOwner`, and `eventName` predicates untouched, per your instruction to keep them behaving as they do now. But per the collation finding above, those reads currently plan as `Index Cond: (domain_id = …)` + `Filter: (target_ref = …)` — the *same* whole-domain scan, on the more common read path. `eventNamePrefix` needs a real decision rather than a mechanical edit, since it uses range comparisons where collation changes ordering semantics. I filed a task chip (`task_1084bbd0`) with the evidence and the plan-gate extension points.</result>

## The headline finding: no selection widening was needed

The brief's premise — "a whole custody transfer commits ONLY `custody:&lt;holdingId&gt;` + `custody:transfer/&lt;requestId&gt;`, no `yi:` effect" — is **stale against this tree**. `yi-runtime-custody-transfer-occasion.ts:170-174` unconditionally pushes `prepareRuntimeYiRootMutationEffect(storage, source.holdingId, { kind: 'advance' })`; git shows the push present since commit `a24384e91 fix(occasion): record replay-complete Yi mutations` and surviving `5c627b189`/`5cbe1fbfa`. Live probe byte evidence (whole transfer commit): `custody:&lt;uid&gt;` custody.transfer + `custody:transfer/&lt;req&gt;` + **`yi:&lt;uid&gt;` kinds.root-advance**. Probes across every owner confirmed the same co-commit law: identity (patch/reparent/suspend/resume/presence via `rootMutation:{kind:'advance'}`), custody (transfer/credit/activate/deactivate; extinguish rides `kinds.root-extinguish`), containment (exclusive-move), relations (create births the root; lifecycle verbs advance it), authority (issuer epochs and certificate issue/revoke/consume all advance their root). **Therefore `commitTargetRef: yi:&lt;uid&gt;` already selects every relevant commit; the whole defect was filter+fold.** `commitTargetRef` stays a single reference; PG SQL unchanged; the plan gate stayed green untouched.

**Custody root-advance recommendation:** nothing to recommend — the transfer already co-commits the root advance, satisfying constitution law 3. Evidence above.

## Filter (exact, never prefix for context owners)

Accepts: `yi:&lt;uid&gt;`, `kinds:&lt;uid&gt;/` prefix, exact `identity:&lt;uid&gt;`, `custody:&lt;uid&gt;`, `containment:&lt;uid&gt;`, `relations:&lt;uid&gt;`, plus `authority:certificate/` prefix — the last because byte evidence shows a certificate-carrying Yi's authority component commits at `authority:certificate/&lt;certId&gt;`, **not** `authority:&lt;uid&gt;` (nothing in the tree targets `authority:&lt;uid&gt;`; `yi-runtime-manifest-effects.ts` overrides the manifest target to the certificate coordinate). Admission for certificate effects is finished in the fold: `canonicalAfterState.rootUid === uid`, else the effect stays an observation — one manifestation commit demonstrably carries certificate effects for *two different Yis* (delegated issuance consumes parent certificates), and rootUid is the only exact discriminator. Excluded: `custody:transfer/…`, `containment:move/…`, `authority:issuer/…`, `kinds:binding…` — proven present in commits and proven not to fold (unit + e2e).

## Known limits (documented divergences, none silent — each either matches live, fails loudly, or is listed here)

1. **Composed binding closure**: non-primary binding addresses are not in commit bytes (see binding-manifest verdict), so `bindings` on multi-binding Yis under-reports vs live (e.g. spirit: fold 2 vs live 7). One-line producer fix for the owner: `contextEffect`'s kinds loop (`yi-runtime-manifest-effects.ts`) building `command` with the per-binding address/id instead of the selection's, and `runtime-relation-prepared-create.ts:110` adding `kindAddress` — both unowned this wave. Probe (d) therefore compares the full row minus `bindings`.
2. **Partial-split credited holding**: its birth commits `kinds.root-birth` + `binding-birth` (no addresses) + `custody.transfer-credit`; no manifest-shaped effect exists, so its at-read returns null ("not manifested in this window") rather than a fabricated image.
3. **Epoch-based authority revocation** is invisible from the revoked Yi's coordinates: the item-transfer commit (dumped) carries no authority effect, yet live `authority.active` flips via the issuer's epoch. Event-time shows `active:true` until a per-certificate effect commits. Direct `certificate-revoked`/`use-consumed` fold exactly.
4. **Container `children`** aggregate other Yis' placement coordinates and never fold (live loadout shows `{containment:{children:[…]}}`).
5. **At-read rows are not address-pathified**: live reads run `projectCurrent`→`pathifyHolding` (e.g. holder `~ctx_bob`), the at-read path returns the folded row unprojected (uids). `pathifyAny(storage, atRow)` yields byte-equality with live (probe b proves it). Fix belongs in unowned files (`views/service/yi-read.ts` readAt, or `yi-runtime-point-read.ts` post-processing) — recommended to the owner.

plan 49, 50, 51, 52 are completed. now I am investigating sdk surface, and api elegance/optimalness

After looking into the sdk, I recognize the current surface is fragmented, and we can create a more unified, compact api, and actually, I am investigating if I should restructure or rewrite some of it 

Core is the dependency constitution beneath the SDK, Std, and Server. If its boundaries are unclear, downstream elegance becomes a façade over broad dependencies and duplicated semantics.
The most important finding is not merely Core’s size:

* Core exposes 49 entrypoints; its root exports 248 runtime values and 294 types.
* Owner paths are inconsistent: `/views` and `/activation` are narrow contracts, while `/authority` and `/identity` pull in most of Runtime and Node dependencies.
* More seriously, World product semantics currently have two owners:
   * SDK’s local implementation: 860 lines.
   * Server’s connected implementation: 758 lines.
* Both independently implement catalog, exact binding, create, verify, invoke, Activation, transfer, and related rules.

The provisional correction is:

```
Core: one access-bound World product execution service
  ├── SDK local adapter
  └── Server RPC adapter

SDK: application-facing World / Kit / Kind / Yi capabilities
Server: authentication, framing, limits, serialization
```

That Core execution object should itself be OCap-shaped: World, actor, presentation, and exact context are fixed when bound; callers cannot substitute them; every operation still re-evaluates current Authority.
I also recorded a provisional Core exposure model:

* Core root: small, portable kernel.
* Owner-named paths: portable contracts, codecs, and pure derivations.
* `/runtime`: explicit host execution.
* `/composition`: host wiring.
* `/adapter-spi/*`: exact adapter ports.
* `/operations/*`: privileged workflows.
* No routinely published `internal` paths.
* Pure Std should not import Core directly.

The full audit, comparisons, alternatives, laws, and open questions are now in [SDK elegance exploration](/Users/ren/repos/bonfire/docs/architecture/sdk-elegance-exploration.md). Core is now explicitly marked as something we must resolve before writing the SDK implementation plan.
Docs verification passed, including hygiene, current-truth, onboarding, and example-index checks.

## Part 3 — Yi row model

### 3.1 The `Yi` type

Defined at `/Users/ren/repos/bonfire/packages/core/src/ports/yi-row.ts:173` (file: 246 lines). Header: `/** Yi — the root substrate type. */`

| Field | Type | One-line meaning (from its doc comment) |
|---|---|---|
| `uid` | `string` | "Opaque, stable, primary key (e.g. `sp_&lt;hex&gt;` / `tk_&lt;hex&gt;`)." |
| `domainId?` | `string` | "Stable logical Domain that owns this root and its Occasion sequence." |
| `$schema?` | `string` | "Dialect version marker for the row's serialization shape" — carries `'bonfire/v1'`. |
| `bindings` | `ReadonlyArray&lt;KindRef&gt;` | "Ordered, additive effective Kind binding addresses" — order drives C3 linearization; first is primary lineage. |
| `primaryBinding` | `string \| null` | "Semantic address of the primary Kind binding." |
| `createdAt` | `string` | Creation instant. |
| `extinguishedAt` | `string \| null` | Extinction instant, or null while live. |
| `seq?` | `number` | "Monotonic per-host sequence number" written on row insert. |
| `occasionHeadId?` | `string` | "Pointer to the most recent Occasion commit for this row"; the discover cache keys on it. |
| `contexts?` | `YiContextComponents` | "Context-owned current facts joined for this read; never authored state." |
| `authoredState` | `YiAuthoredState` | "Kind-namespaced row data. Every kind on the row contributes a single bucket keyed by its `KindRef`." |

Two companion interfaces live in the same file: `YiAuthoredState` (line 46, an open `Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;` with two hard-coded product buckets `'core:membered'` and `'core:streamed'`) and `YiContextComponents` (line 104, with `identity` / `custody` / `containment` / `relations` / `authority` sub-shapes). `YiIdentity` (line 222) is a separate mutable-shaped identity value.

## 4. Deviations, and the `worldAuthorityIssue` decision

- **`InvokeYiOpts.presentedCertificate` renamed to `certificate`, not deleted.** `invokeYi` is the recorded `dispatchChokepoint`: it decides whether `(target, method)` is a declared port or a built-in context verb, and *that decision is the operation identity Authority evaluates*. Deleting the field would force the Server to duplicate that dispatch decision before it could name a `PortInvocationOperation`. The field now carries the one presented certificate straight into `executePresentedWorldInvocation` — one evaluator, one presentation per access. Law 3's actual defect (a certificate travelling through nested command-option bags into `assertCan`) is fully gone: `RuntimeCommandOptions` and every service opts bag lost the field.
- **New `InvocationShape` (`'targeted' | 'listing'`).** Law 4 as written is unimplementable without it: a listing read targets the World root, and asserting `identity.descendantOf` selectors against that root denies every narrowed certificate. `authorizeWorldInvocation` now takes `shape`, skips resource assertion for `'listing'`, and records it in the decision (and in the resume digest, so a listing decision cannot be replayed as a targeted one). Verified by test.
- **Camel-case coverage names.** Lane 1 canonicalised operation names (`holdings.verifyProof` → `holdings.verify-proof`); lane 3 did not, and the at-rest codec forbids uppercase. Left alone, every api key minted with a camel-case scope would have stopped matching its own call. `canonicalAuthorityOperationName` now lives in `authority/contracts/certificate-issued.ts` and is used by **both** `methodAllowed` and `issueWorldAuthorityCertificate`; the Server's duplicate copy is deleted and imports the Core one.
- **`explainWriteAuthz` lost its `opts` rather than being rewritten over `explainWorldInvocation`.** It explains the *structural write floor gate* (lane 4), not the certificate lane; the certificate lane's explanation already **is** `explainWorldInvocation`. No production or test caller passed `presentedCertificate`. `create-yi-runtime.ts` now passes `currentInvocationAuthority()?.subject ?? caller`, keeping Authority's ambient envelope out of `authority/service` (owner boundary).
- **`presented-watch.ts` kept its own two `authorizeWorldInvocation` calls.** The generalization landed as `presentedCertificateSubject` in the Server adapter (used by `addressing.ts`, `chat-typing.ts`, `trace.ts`). `presented-watch` needs the whole decision (`audienceHost`, `eventsAllow`), not just the subject, so folding it into a subject-returning helper would have lost information.
- **Renames to satisfy the literal done-when grep**: `presentedCertificateIds` → `certificateIds` (Authority decision context, 8 files, not persisted) and `presentedCertificates(access)` → `accessCertificates(access)`. This also renamed the **wire field** `authority.explain` `presentedCertificates` → `certificates`, matching `world.authority.explain`. SDK + Server updated together.
- **`worldAuthorityIssue`: left alone — it is not a second conjunctive evaluator.** `admitCurrentParentChain` answers "may these bytes be written as a child of that parent": parent liveness/activity, cycle and depth bounds, caller-controls-parent, endpoint liveness, issuer-epoch currency, and `authorityDelegationFailureCode` (coverage containment, validity containment, attenuation/transfer rank, Domain co-location). It never evaluates a request target, never asserts resource selectors against a coordinate, never consumes audience or use-budget caveats, and produces no subject substitution. Critically, `authorizeWorldInvocation` **already calls the same `authorityDelegationFailureCode`** at every chain step, so the containment predicate has exactly one implementation. Routing issuance through a `delegate`-shaped operation would need a target Yi that does not exist and would burn caveats an issuance must not consume. The authority to issue comes from controlling the parent — the object-capability law — and that is what `requireParentControllerCaller` enforces.
- **`packages.rollback`** got `{ owner: 'packages', target: &lt;the install's Yi&gt; }` from the existing `resolvePackageLifecycleTarget`; no new Core semantic was needed.
- Tombstone headers ("Extracted from the historical monolithic method table") fixed in the 4 kit/package files this change touched; 5 identical copies remain in files I did not touch (sub-plan 09's territory).

## 5. Where the spec was wrong about the code

- **`assertCan`'s `presentedCertificate` was not a parameter to drop but a whole option object to delete.** `AuthOpts` had no other live consumer, so the 5th parameter went entirely (20 call sites).
- **Law 4 is not implementable without a listing/targeted distinction** (see above). The spec assumes passing the World root as target is sufficient; it is not — the selectors deny it.
- **`resolveHoldsProof` is not unused** (`gates/caller-authorized-leaf.ts` imports it dynamically). Kept. `presentedHoldingSource` and `resolveDelegationProof` were dead and are gone.
- **The done-when grep matches `presentedCertificateIds` and the `presentedCertificates(access)` helper sub-plan 01 introduced.** Resolved by renaming both.
- **`explainWriteAuthz` cannot be rewritten over `explainWorldInvocation`** — different lane (see above).
- **The Server's api-key mint compiles scopes to kebab-case**, which only lane 1 understood; the spec does not mention it and it would have silently broken every camel-case api key.
- Step 10's file list is stale in places (`callers.ts:91–108` etc. were already gone); I fixed the comment-rule violations that actually exist in the files this change touches.

## 6. Behavior a product user would notice

1. **A narrowed certificate now narrows reads.** Previously a certificate scoped to `descendantOf: X` (or any resource selector) was World-wide on every RPC read, on manifestation, on API-key authentication, and on typing signals. Now: a targeted read outside the scope is `PermissionDenied`; a listing read returns only rows the selectors admit; an API-key bearer bound to a narrowed certificate cannot widen through `yi.where`. This is the intended, deliberate change.
2. **Audience caveats are now enforced on reads and commands** — a certificate bound to another host is denied here.
3. **`setIdentity` under a certificate no longer depends on a predicate mismatch (D8).** `builtinSemanticOwner` and the dispatch arm now share `carriesIdentityProfile`, so a transient-kind row is evaluated for the operation that actually runs.
4. **Authentication is decoupled from authorization.** `assertAuthorityCertificateCurrent` proves an api key or account bearer still stands (liveness, validity window, subject, issuer epoch, expiry caveat) and no longer probes a fabricated action; each call's action and target are decided when the call arrives. An api key whose *first* coverage action happened to fail the old probe now authenticates and is decided per operation instead.
5. **Wire change**: `authority.explain`'s request field `presentedCertificates` is now `certificates`. The SDK snapshot is regenerated at protocol **168**; the wire diff (this rename plus sub-plan 01's package-type renames) needs the protocol bump that sub-plan 11 owns, together with the `llms.txt` / onboarding-probe doc pins (D14).
6. **`agents.runTurn`/`agents.streamTurn`, `yi.traceInvoke`, WS typing signals, and WS subscriptions** now evaluate their certificate against the exact target they act on, so a certificate that does not cover that coordinate is denied where it previously passed.</result>

**The one Server→SDK edge, concretely.** In `packages/package-structure.json`, `packages.server.allowedWorkspaceImports` becomes:

```
["@bonfire/core", "@bonfire/sdk/products", "@bonfire/std/recipes",
 "@bonfire/std/social", "@bonfire/std/agent", "@bonfire/std/sigil",
 "@bonfire/std/community", "@bonfire/std/incubator", "@bonfire/std/examples"]
```

For this to validate, A6's extension must (a) match a subpath entry against a specifier by exact-or-prefix, and (b) derive the *package-name* set for `validateWorkspaceDependencies` by taking the first two segments of each entry (`@bonfire/sdk`, `@bonfire/std`), so `packages/server/package.json`'s `workspace:*` deps (`@bonfire/core`, `@bonfire/sdk`, `@bonfire/std`) still equal the expected set. Recording the edge as a bare `@bonfire/sdk` entry would silently re-admit `substrate`, `advanced`, and the root — the exact defect law 3 exists to prevent.

**Done-when grep (from the spec, verified executable):**
`grep -rn "from '@bonfire/sdk" packages/server/src --include='*.ts' | grep -v test | grep -v "@bonfire/sdk/products"` — note `grep -v test` also drops `packages/server/src/testing/**` and every `@bonfire/sdk/testing` line, so it will pass while those survive. That is consistent with law 4 (test-support is Server-owned) but the grep does not prove it.

#### T6 — Purity test and gate retirement (steps 6, 7, law 6)

**Modifies:** `packages/std/src/std-surface-inventory.test.ts` (67).

**Design, concretely.** Reuse `scripts/lib/browser-entry-graph.mjs` (298 lines, created by lane A1) exactly as `packages/core/src/public-surface.test.ts:253–261` and `packages/sdk/src/public-surface.test.ts:93–105` already do. The helper takes an arbitrary rule array, so Std supplies its own:

```
const STD_PURITY_RULES = [
  { kind: 'Node built-in',  pattern: /(?:^|[\0:])node:/ },
  { kind: '@bonfire/core',  pattern: /(?:^|[/\\])packages[/\\]core[/\\](?:src|dist)[/\\]/ },
  { kind: 'SDK host path',  pattern: /(?:^|[/\\])packages[/\\]sdk[/\\](?:src|dist)[/\\](?:substrate|advanced|host|testing)(?:[/\\.]|$)/ },
]
```

then, for every row of `packages/std/public-entrypoints.json`:
`createEntryGraphReader({ tsconfigPath: &lt;repo&gt;/tsconfig.base.json })` → `valueGraphOf(join(stdSrc, source))` → `browserSafetyViolations(graph, STD_PURITY_RULES)` → `expect(...).toEqual([])`, formatted with `formatBrowserSafetyViolations`. Because the helper resolves through `tsconfig.base.json` `paths`, `@bonfire/sdk/substrate` resolves to `packages/sdk/src/substrate.ts` and matches the third rule as a workspace path; `@bonfire/sdk/host` will resolve once 07/S18 creates it. Type-only edges are erased (`importCarriesValue`, `:105–121`), so `import type` of an SDK host type costs nothing — which is what law 2 intends. Per the spec's own note, no separate side-effect assertion is needed: a graph with no Core or Runtime module cannot register anything.

**Gate retirement (three files, one change):** `package.json:25` (`check:std-structure`), `scripts/check-release.mjs:38`, `scripts/check-changed.mjs:301`; delete `scripts/check-std-static-substrate-install.mjs` (45). **Plus the file neither spec names:** `packages/sdk/src/release-gate-checker.test.ts:114` (`['check:std-structure']` in the pinned order).

## 0. Framing constraints that shape these lanes

Eight verified properties of the current code and gate set.

1. **`packages/core/structure-map.json` grants are exact in both directions.** `scripts/check-core-structure.mjs:333–344` errors on an *unused* grant as well as a missing one, and the `world` shell's grant list (`structure-map.json:1576–1635`) currently names 8 contexts and 2 shells. Every new Core import that `world/service/` makes — `kinds/service/deployment/*`, `kinds/service/revision-binding/resolve-binding-v2.ts`, `kinds/contracts/interface/revision.ts`, `kinds/contracts/presentation/revision.ts`, `runtime/composition/kinds.ts`, `runtime/composition/package-management/package-{publish,install,update,uninstall,discovery}.ts`, `packages/contracts/release-types.ts` — must be added in the same lane. Verified no cycle risk: nothing under `runtime/`, `kinds/`, or `compiler/` imports `../world/`.
2. **`world` is a *shell*, so its files get `otherLineLimit: 1000`** (`check-core-structure.mjs:220–232`; semantic 600-line limit applies only to kernel, contexts, and the `compiler`/`ports` shells). `world/service/packages.ts` is 468 lines — there is room, but `define`/`undefine`/`describe`/`lift` belong in new files, not appended there.
3. **`packages/sdk/src/world/structure.test.ts:47–59` caps every production leaf in `packages/sdk/src/world/` at 1,000 lines and 64 KiB and requires an exact `(./name.ts)` route in `packages/sdk/src/world/README.md` (32 lines).** `product.ts` is 968 lines against that ceiling; S3 splits it. Every new World file this sub-plan adds needs a README line in the same lane.
4. **Adding an RPC method reddens three pins in the same change**: `packages/sdk/src/client/rpc-schema-structure.test.ts:25–26` (`EXPECTED_RUNTIME_ORDER_HASH`, currently `a8e1b036…`), `:84` (schema key order must equal `packages/sdk/public-types-snapshot/wire.json`'s 140 method keys), and `packages/sdk/src/client/rpc-schema/README.md` routing if a new context file is added. `BONFIRE_SERVER_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays **168** in this sub-plan — C1 (11) owns the bump to 169.
5. **A private-Kit release id today embeds the content digest.** `privateKitReleaseId` (`packages/core/src/world/service/packages.ts:167–185`) returns `pkg:&lt;publisher&gt;.kit-&lt;digest.slice(0,40)&gt;`; `packages/sdk/src/world/product.ts:510–518` versions it `0.0.0+${digest.slice(0,20)}`. `comparePackageSemver` (`package-semver.ts:23–30`) is fed by `parsePackageSemver` (`:11–21`), whose regex `(?:\+[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?` **discards build metadata** — so every re-publication of an edited Kit compares equal *and* lands under a different `packageId`. That is exactly D22's "re-installing an edited Kit creates a second package".
6. **`packages.publish` requires a *root* publisher and caller-is-owner.** `packagePublisherIdentity` (`package-publish-support.ts:66–93`) refuses any principal that is not `@world` with `namespace.length === 0` or `~identity`, and requires `publisherHandle === pkg.publisher`. `worldPackagePublish` (`world/service/packages.ts:63–73`) refuses when `subject !== owner`. Both bind law 11's release-identity design (see correction **C2**).
7. **A changed redeploy of a live family is refused today.** `packages/core/src/kinds/service/revision-binding/sealed-portable-proof-source.ts:81–103` (`restoreExactSealedPortableLineage`) throws unless the stored lineage's single entry names the *same* `revisionId`. **K5 lifts this.** Until K5 lands, transcripts T6/T7 cannot pass, and the membership-staleness defect in §4 D3 stays latent.
8. **`prepareKindInstallPlanV1` refuses every migration.** `packages/core/src/kinds/service/deployment/kind-install-plan.ts:38–45` throws `FeatureNotSupported` when `migrations.size &gt; 0`; `package-discovery.ts:246–279` does the same for package definitions. **K5 deletes both.**

"After K5" below means the lane's tests exercise a *changed* redeploy of a live family. "After K10" means the lane touches a `gates` literal or the `gates` key on the Kind execution manifest.

| **N9** | Agents tool + `docs/examples/dynamic-kinds` | step 7 | N8 | ∥ N10 | 1 | +6 / 4 / 0 |
| **N10** | The eleven transcripts, local and connected | step 8 | N8 | ∥ N9 | 2 | +3 / 2 / 0 |

**Total 16.5 agent-days** (the spec prices 10–15; see correction **C10**).
Critical path: `N1 → N5 → N6 → N8 → N10` = 9.5 d; `N3 → N5` and `N4 → N5` join early; `N2` is free after S6/K10.

### 1.1 Transcript coverage map

Step 8 lists **eleven** semicolon-separated clauses, not nine (correction **C11**). Numbering them T1…T11:

| # | transcript | lane that makes it pass | local | connected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | a member with a define certificate defines `@hearth.forge:ticket` | N10 (needs N1, N2, N5, N8) | ✓ | ✓ |
| T2 | another member sees it through `open('@hearth.forge')` and creates one | N10 (needs N2, N8) | ✓ | ✓ |
| T3 | a third without access sees nothing | N10 (needs N2 `discover` filter) | ✓ | ✓ |
| T4 | `describe()` returns the schemas and explanations the definer wrote | N6 (unit) + N10 | ✓ | ✓ |
| T5 | `vip-ticket extends ticket` found by a View over `ticket` and a `bears(ticket)` gate | N3 (unit, depth 3) + N10 | ✓ | ✓ |
| T6 | a compatible redefinition of `ticket` changes behavior of existing `vip-ticket` instances | N4 (unit) + N5 + N10 | ✓ | ✓ |
| T7 | an incompatible one is refused with the breakage list | N5 (unit) + N10 | ✓ | ✓ |
| T8 | two concurrent defines of one name yield one live install | N5 (unit) + N10 | ✓ | ✓ (PG only) |
| T9 | `undefine(ticket)` refused while `vip-ticket` exists | N5 (unit) + N10 | ✓ | ✓ |
| T10 | extinguish then undefine succeed in order | N5 (unit) + N10 | ✓ | ✓ |
| T11 | a `lift` of the two Kinds installs as a Kit in another World | N6 + N8 + N10 | ✓ | ✓ |

### N4 — re-point survivability
**Spec:** law 6 ("re-pointing a parent re-points children's parent binding"), law 8. **Depends on:** K5. **Concurrent with** N1, N2, N3.

This lane exists because of a defect the current refusal hides (§4 **D3**). `YiBindingMembershipStateV1` (`packages/core/src/kinds/service/ports/yi-representation-repository.ts:33–38`) stores `bindingRevisionId` per row, but a compatible redeploy only rewrites the **address selection** (`putBindingAddress`, `runtime/composition/kind-binding-catalog.ts:60–65`). `assertBearsInstalledKind` (`packages/core/src/world/service/installed-kind.ts:63–66`) then compares the row's stale membership revision against the freshly selected one and throws `KindNotFound`. Today `sealed-portable-proof-source.ts:81–103` refuses the redeploy so this never fires; **K5 removes the refusal and this becomes T6's failure mode.**

Creates:
- `packages/core/src/world/service/installed-kind.test.ts` — a row manifested under revision *N* still satisfies `assertBearsInstalledKind` after the address re-points to *N+1*, and a row that never bore the binding still fails.

Modifies:
- `packages/core/src/world/service/installed-kind.ts` (106) — `assertBearsInstalledKind` (`:57–76`) proves membership by `bindingId` (durable identity) and reports the revision only in the failure details. The *descriptor* staleness check stays where it belongs, in `assertInstalledKindRef` (`:22–49`), which already throws `Conflict('kind_binding_not_current')` — that is law 8's exactness, and it is unchanged.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/composition/kind-binding-catalog.ts` (274) — the `putBindingAddress` loop at `:55–79` also invalidates `registry.portableSelection` so `resolveRuntimeKindBindingSelection` (`:82–95`) does not serve the hot pre-repoint selection. **This is the second half of D23 that K1 explicitly deferred** ("K8 must resolve manifest from committed state / invalidate"); coordinate with K8 so only one lane writes it.
- `packages/server/src/manifestation-parity.integration.test.ts` — add the re-point arm to the PG side.

### N5 — Core `define`/`undefine`
**Spec:** step 1 (the `define`/`undefine` half); laws 1, 6, 7, 11. **Depends on:** N1, N3, N4.

Creates:
- `packages/core/src/world/contracts/define.ts` — `KindDeclaration` (the portable single-family lowering; structurally `PortableKitFamilyInstallSourceV3` from `packages/sdk/src/authoring/portable-kit-install-source-v3.ts:92–105`, restated as a Core contract so `@bonfire/core/world` stays browser-safe — declare it structurally or import type-only, since `scripts/lib/browser-entry-graph.mjs:114,131` drops type-only edges), `WorldDefineInput/Result`, `WorldUndefineInput/Result`.
- `packages/core/src/world/service/define.ts` — `worldDefine` and `worldUndefine`.
- `packages/core/src/world/service/define.test.ts`.

`worldDefine` runs **one** `executeWorldSemanticCommand(host, { access, owner:'kinds', target: &lt;namespace principal uid&gt;, method:'kinds.define' }, …)` and inside the body, with `caller = subject`:
1. derives the release coordinate — `pkg:&lt;root handle&gt;.kind-&lt;40 hex of the canonical Kind address&gt;` and version `0.0.&lt;n&gt;` where `n = (parsePackageSemver(latest?.version)?.patch ?? 0) + 1` from `host.packages.get({ packageId })` (`package-discovery.ts:109–131`, which returns the most recently published manifest). **Not `pkg:&lt;owner path&gt;.&lt;kind name&gt;`** — see correction **C2**;
2. mints a family genesis when the declaration carries none (`createKindFamily`, `packages/core/src/kinds/contracts/family.ts:77–90`, needs only a random `klin_`/`knonce_` pair — cf. `packages/sdk/src/tools/family-registry-cli.ts:36–37`) and **persists it in the declaration written into the release**, so `lift()` returns it;
3. publishes through `host.packages.publish` with `ownerSpirit = &lt;the namespace's root principal&gt;` (forced by `packagePublisherIdentity`, `package-publish-support.ts:66–93`), tolerating the `PayloadInvalid` duplicate at `package-publish.ts:191–199` by re-reading and bumping `n` once, then failing `Conflict` (**T8**);
4. installs or updates: `host.packages.install(…, options)` first; on `PayloadInvalid { reason:'package_already_installed' }` (`package-install.ts:439–450` and `:678–693`) switch to `host.packages.update({ installedTo: worldRootUid, packageId, version }, options)` (`package-update.ts:70–120`). `packageUpdate`'s downgrade guard (`package-update-support.ts:120–140`) is satisfied because `0.0.&lt;n&gt;` increases monotonically — which is precisely why law 11 replaces `0.0.0+&lt;digest&gt;`;
5. surfaces an incompatible redefinition as the `SchemaIncompatible` raised at `kind-install-plan.ts:160–170`, whose details already carry `breakages` (**T7**).

`worldUndefine` runs `kinds.undefine` against the same target and calls `host.packages.uninstall`, which already carries both guards: `assertNoExternalLiveRowsForDeployedKinds` → `package_kind_live_rows` (`package-uninstall.ts:304–320`, **T10**) and `assertNoDependentPackageInstalls` → `package_reverse_dependency` (`:407–428`, **T9**). The child's dependency edge is created by recording the parent's release in the child's `dependsOn`; note the reverse-dependency match is `entry.packageId === record.packageId &amp;&amp; entry.hash === record.manifestHash` (`:415–416`), so a parent re-point breaks the link — **this lane must match on `packageId` alone for namespace-defined releases** (§4 **D4**).

Modifies:
- `packages/core/src/world/service/bind.ts` (236) — `define`, `undefine` on `WorldExecution` (interface `:76–127`, implementation `:137–210`); both take the host-supplied `WorldPackageOperationOptions` (`world/service/packages.ts:44–45`), exactly like `packageInstall` does at `:201–203`, because the portable→candidate lowering lives in the SDK (correction **C6**).
- `packages/core/src/world/service/packages.ts` (468) — `privateKitReleaseId` (`:167–185`) gains the `kind-&lt;digest&gt;` form and drops the `kit-&lt;digest&gt;` content dependence in favour of the Kit's `definitionId`; `privateKitDigest` (`:188–190`) survives for the *lock fingerprint*, not the id.
- `packages/core/src/world/contracts/operations.ts` (206), `packages/core/src/api/world.ts` (80), `packages/core/src/api/runtime.ts` (204).
- `packages/core/structure-map.json` — `world` grants gain `runtime/composition/package-management/package-{publish,install,update,uninstall,discovery}.ts` and `kinds/service/deployment/kind-validation.ts`.
- `packages/core/src/public-api-snapshot.json`, `packages/core/src/public-types-snapshot.json`.
- `packages/sdk/src/world/product.ts` (968) `:508–518` — the Kit release id/version move to the law-11 form (this hunk is inside the block S3 moves to `packages/sdk/src/world/kit-binding.ts`; **collision, §4 X1**).

### N6 — `describe()` and `lift()`
**Spec:** step 1 (the `describe`/`lift` half); law 10. **Depends on:** N5, and on K4's survivor set. **Concurrent with** N7.

Creates:
- `packages/core/src/world/contracts/describe.ts` — `KindDescription { declaration, interface, presentation, examples, facets, access, binding }`.
- `packages/core/src/world/service/describe.ts` — `worldDescribeKind`, `worldLiftKind`.
- `packages/core/src/world/service/describe.test.ts`.

Reads, all verified reachable:
- **declaration, schema, ports, gates, examples, composeAddresses** — `resolveKind(host.storage, kindAddress)` then `projectReadableKind` (`packages/core/src/world/service/readable-kind.ts:23–68`, 114 lines). `ReadableKind` (`world/contracts/readable-kind.ts:6–25`) already carries `examples`, `gates`, `ports`, `rowSchema`, `lifecycle`, `events`, `composeAddresses`, `defaultsByAddress`. `describe()` is mostly an assembly over an existing projection.
- **binding coordinates and facet expansions** — `host.storage.yiRepresentation.bindingRuntime(kindAddress)` → `YiKindBindingRuntimeStateV1` (`kinds/service/ports/yi-representation-repository.ts:56–61`: `executionManifest`, `representationPlan`, `contributions`).
- **interface revision** — `resolveKindBindingRevisionV2(store, bindingRevisionId)` (`packages/core/src/kinds/service/revision-binding/resolve-binding-v2.ts:37–…`, 191 lines, a **K4 survivor**) yields `body.interfaceRevisionId` (`kinds/contracts/composition/binding-revision-v2.ts:57`), then `store.readImmutableRecord('interface-revision', id)` → `decodeKindInterfaceEnvelopeV1` (`kinds/contracts/interface/revision.ts:79–…`, 248 lines). The store is `resolveKindRevisionBindingStoreV2(host.storage)` (`runtime/composition/kinds.ts:105,226,481`).
- **presentation revision** — **no stored pointer exists** (§4 **D5**): `KindBindingRevisionBodyV2` carries `interfaceRevisionId` but not `presentationRevisionId`; the only writer is `admit-repository-v2.ts:360–364`, keyed by the content digest `kprs_&lt;hash(envelope)&gt;`. Read it from `manifest.definition.families[i].surface.presentation` (`packages/sdk/src/authoring/portable-kit-install-source-v3.ts:92–96`, written into the manifest by `worldPackagePublish`), recompute the id, and read the persisted record back by that id to prove agreement. Do **not** add a field to the binding-revision body — that changes an immutable digest domain.
- **access gates in explained form** — the same normalizer `assertPolicyScopesResolvable` uses (`kind-validation.ts:173`, `boundaryPorts.authority.normalizeGate`).

`worldLiftKind` resolves the live install for the Kind address (`liveWorldPackageInstalls`, `world/service/installed-kind.ts:92–106`), reads `manifest.definition`, and returns the matching `families[]` entry plus its genesis. Both operations run under `executeWorldSemanticCommand({ owner:'kinds', target: &lt;kind's install target&gt;, method:'kinds.describe' | 'kinds.lift' })` **and** the same `discover` probe the catalog uses (`world/service/catalog.ts:207–228`) — see §4 **D6** for why they must not follow `kinds.get`'s precedent.

### 3.5 `actFor` certificate shape

`WorldAuthorityIssueInput.ceremony: 'grant-to' | 'act-for'` (`world/contracts/operations.ts:133`). `worldAuthorityIssue` (`world/service/authority.ts:33–68`) sets `presenter = access.actor` for `act-for` and `subject = input.subject`. `issueWorldAuthorityCertificate` (`runtime/composition/world-authority.ts:125–175`) lowers `actions[].port` through `canonicalAuthorityOperationName` into `{ kind:'method', name }` selectors (`:147–149`). `methodAllowed` (`world-authority-evaluation.ts:823–833`) matches exact `method`, `method-namespace` by `prefix`/`prefix.`, or `action: 'method.invoke'`. The SDK issues it at `packages/sdk/src/world/authority.ts:103` (`this.issue('act-for', subject, spec)`). Resource narrowing is by `identity` / `custody` / `containment` / `relation` selectors only — **there is no Kind-namespace resource selector**, which is why the define right narrows by naming `kinds.define` as the *action* and the namespace principal as the *subject*.

## 4. Corrections and conflicts

### Corrections to the spec

**C1 — "make the deploy path pass the ambient subject" is one line in the SDK and one in the Server, not a Core change.** `worldPackageInstall` (`world/service/packages.ts:111–114`) *already* passes `{ subject: caller }` from `executeWorldSemanticCommand`, and `installPackage` already forwards it as `context.installer` (`package-install.ts:174`). The break is downstream: `packages/sdk/src/authoring/runtime-package-lifecycle.ts:126` passes `activeContext.targetUid` and `packages/server/src/methods/packages/lifecycle.ts:123` passes `{ asCaller: context.targetUid }` — i.e. **every package-borne Kind deploy today runs its owner-authority check as the World root, not as the caller.** `kits.deploy` does it correctly (`packages/server/src/methods/kits/deploy.ts:123, :298` use `methodSubject` / `callers.subject`). Fixing this is a real behaviour change: an install whose Kinds are owned outside the installer's subtree begins failing. N1 owns it and owns the fixture updates.

**C2 — the release id in law 11 cannot be spelled `pkg:&lt;owner path&gt;.&lt;kind name&gt;`.** `parsePackageAddress` (`address-parser.ts:289–303`) splits the body on `.` and requires exactly two parts, each matching `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$/` — no `@`, no `~`, no second dot. `pkg:@hearth.forge.ticket` throws on both counts. Additionally `packagePublisherIdentity` (`package-publish-support.ts:66–93`) requires the publisher to be a **root** `@world` (namespace length 0) or `~identity` whose handle equals `pkg.publisher`, and `worldPackagePublish` refuses `subject !== owner` (`world/service/packages.ts:67–73`). **Proposed resolution, one owner per semantic:** the release id is `pkg:&lt;root handle&gt;.kind-&lt;40 hex of the canonical Kind address&gt;` (mirroring the existing `kit-&lt;digest&gt;` convention at `world/service/packages.ts:184`), version `0.0.&lt;n&gt;`; the release *owner* is the namespace's root principal; and `worldDefine` performs the publish/install/update **inside** the `kinds.define` decision through `host.packages.*` rather than re-entering `worldPackagePublish`, so there is exactly one authorization (`kinds.define` against the namespace target, plus `resolveKindInstallOwnerAuthority` inside the deploy). Add a test that a define under `@hearth.forge` cannot mint a release under any other `pkg:hearth.*` coordinate.

**C3 — `advanced(world).namespaces` cannot create a namespace today.** `packages/sdk/src/advanced/index.ts:23–25` exposes only `{ main }`, and `main` is the constitutional `@&lt;slug&gt;.app` row minted at World bootstrap (`packages/sdk/src/world/local-world.ts:38–51`). There is no Core operation that creates `@hearth.forge`; the only creators are `packages/server/src/methods/packages/materialization.ts:346–382` (`SYSTEM_CALLER`, package-owned) and `packages/sdk/src/testing/substrate.ts:150–185` (test fixture). N2 adds `worldCreateNamespace` plus one RPC method; the spec prices this at zero.

**C4 — "the deploy path resolves nothing against the installed catalog" is false.** `closeRuntimeExternalBindingsV2` (`kind-install-compiler-closure.ts:49–133`) resolves every external `composes` address through `boundaryPorts.catalogs.resolveBindingSelection` → `resolveRuntimeKindBindingSelection` (`kind-binding-catalog.ts:82–95`) and re-compiles with the closed context; it is called on all three deploy entries (`kind-deployment.ts:131, :194, :307`). Step 4's clause "have the deploy path supply external selections for parents outside the install set" is already implemented. What is genuinely missing is (a) transitive closure (D1) and (b) a *visibility* check — law 5's "Parents must be visible to the definer at define time" has no implementation; `resolveBindingSelection` ignores the `discover` gate. N3 adds the visibility probe.

**C5 — "the compiler gains a schema-widening comparator beside the compatibility check" overstates the work.** `checkCompatibility(parent, child, 'backward')` in `packages/core/src/compiler/schema/evolution.ts:252–273` already *is* the widening relation, with `BreakageReason` and `formatBreakages` (`:280–285`). N3 ships a named wrapper and its call site, not a new engine.

**C6 — Core's World service cannot compile a portable declaration by itself.** `installPackage` requires an injected `prepareDefinitionInstall` (`package-install.ts:160–177`), and the portable→candidate lowering — including the construction of the interface and presentation envelopes — lives in the **SDK** at `packages/sdk/src/authoring/portable-kit-install-source-v3.ts:413–760` (903 lines) and `-v4.ts` (209). Step 1's "`define` compiles one portable declaration" must be read as "`define` runs the existing Core install ingress over already-lowered `KindDeclaration` bytes, with the host-supplied continuation" — consistent with README law 10 ("`KindDeclaration` is the portable lowering"). `WorldExecution.define` therefore takes `WorldPackageOperationOptions` exactly as `packageInstall` does.

**C7 — `yi.read({ as: Parent })` needs no wire change.** `ReadableYi.authoredState` is already Kind-address-keyed and `ReadableYi.bindings` already carries the whole lineage (`world/contracts/readable-yi.ts:120–137`). What *is* wrong today is `snapshotOf` at `packages/sdk/src/world/product.ts:941–943`, which returns the leaf bucket only rather than the leaf-wins merge law 5 promises.

**C8 — `Yi&lt;Sword&gt;` cannot expose the merged action surface from today's catalog.** `WorldCatalogKind` (`world/contracts/catalog.ts:44–58`) has no `composes`, and `catalogInstallation` (`world/service/catalog.ts:100–109`) builds `actions` from the leaf Kind's own `readable.ports` — the execution manifest is `{ ...source }` (`compile-one.ts:120–125`), never the composed chain. Step 5's merged surface requires adding `composes` to the catalog descriptor and merging client-side. (Dispatch itself is already correct: `port-resolution.ts` walks all bindings last-match-wins.)

**C9 — line-number drift, all minor.** `runtime/query/read.ts` `discover` loop is at `:249–265`, not `:247–250`. `admit-repository-v2.ts` interface/presentation records are at `:356–365`, not `:357–359`. `port-resolution.ts` last-match-wins is at `:41–44` and `:118–122`. `runtime-product.ts:683,713` no longer exists — 01 replaced it with `liveWorldPackageInstalls` (`world/service/installed-kind.ts:92–106`) filtered on `packageInstallsByTarget(worldUid)`. `privatePackageId` does not exist; the function is `privateKitReleaseId` (`world/service/packages.ts:167`).

**C10 — size.** 16.5 agent-days against the spec's 10–15. The overrun is C3 (namespace creation), C8 (catalog `composes` + client merge), D1 (transitive closure), D3 (membership re-point), and the eleven transcripts run twice.

**C11 — the transcript count.** Step 8 lists **eleven** semicolon-separated clauses; the sub-plan header and README §"End-to-end verification" both say "nine". Use the eleven-row table in §1.1 and amend the two counts in the same landing.

### New defects this analysis found

**D1 — `composes` is never transitively flattened for authored Kinds.** `compile-one.ts:105–110` maps each entry 1:1 to a dependency reference, and `yi-runtime-manifest.ts:180–184` explicitly declines to recurse because "the substrate-seed composes lists already pre-flatten the C3 chain". An authored `C extends B`, `B extends A` therefore yields memberships `[C, B]` — `bears(A)` and a View over `A` miss the instance, breaking law 5 and **T5** at depth 3. Owner: N3 (flatten at compile time; keep manifestation non-recursive).

**D2 — a redeploy never checks the `composes` set.** `prepareCompiledKindDeployment` (`kind-install-plan.ts:136–178`) compares only `evolutionPolicy` and `rowSchema`. Removing a parent on redeploy is silently accepted while live rows still carry the parent membership. Owner: N3.

**D3 — a compatible redeploy strands every existing instance's membership revision.** `installRuntimeKindBindingCatalogV1` rewrites only the address selection (`kind-binding-catalog.ts:55–79`); `YiBindingMembershipStateV1.bindingRevisionId` (`yi-representation-repository.ts:33–38`) keeps the old value; `assertBearsInstalledKind` (`installed-kind.ts:63–66`) then throws `KindNotFound` on the first `world.invoke` or `world.verifyYi` after the re-point. Latent today only because `sealed-portable-proof-source.ts:81–103` refuses the redeploy; **K5 makes it live.** Owner: N4.

**D4 — the reverse-dependency guard breaks on a parent re-point.** `assertNoDependentPackageInstalls` (`package-uninstall.ts:415–416`) matches `entry.packageId === record.packageId &amp;&amp; entry.hash === record.manifestHash`. Re-pointing the parent changes its `manifestHash`, so the child's recorded dependency stops matching and `undefine(parent)` would succeed while children exist — the exact inverse of law 7.
